proofs.full_local_argument: Fix beta>0. Choose u0 in X. Lipschitz continuity gives f(u)>=f(u0)-L||u-u0||. Therefore f(u)+(beta/2)||x-u||^2 tends to infinity along unbounded sequences in X. It is continuous on the closed set X, so it attains a minimum. Convexity of f and strict convexity of the quadratic give uniqueness, denoted p=p_beta(x). For any u in X and t in (0,1], minimality at p and convexity at p+t(u-p) imply 0<=t(f(u)-f(p))-beta*t<x-p,u-p>+(beta*t^2/2)||u-p||^2. Divide by t and let t decrease to zero: f(u)>=f(p)+beta<x-p,u-p>. For q=p_beta(y), apply this inequality at (x,p,u=q) and (y,q,u=p), then add. The result is <x-y,p-q>>=||p-q||^2. Write h=x-y and r=(x-p)-(y-q). Then ||r||^2=||h||^2+||p-q||^2-2<h,p-q><=||h||^2. Thus the residual x-p_beta(x) is 1-Lipschitz. Define g(x)=beta(x-p_beta(x)). Evaluating the minimization defining E_beta(y) at p_beta(x) gives E_beta(y)<=E_beta(x)+<g(x),y-x>+(beta/2)||y-x||^2. Interchanging x,y also gives E_beta(y)>=E_beta(x)+<g(y),y-x>-(beta/2)||y-x||^2. Since ||g(y)-g(x)||<=beta||y-x||, these inequalities imply that E_beta(y)-E_beta(x)-<g(x),y-x> is between -(3beta/2)||y-x||^2 and (beta/2)||y-x||^2. Hence E_beta is differentiable with gradient g, and the residual bound proves beta-smoothness. Finally let x in X. Choosing u=x proves E_beta(x)<=f(x). For every u in X, Lipschitz continuity yields f(u)+(beta/2)||x-u||^2>=f(x)-L||x-u||+(beta/2)||x-u||^2>=f(x)-L^2/(2beta), by completing the square in ||x-u||. Taking the infimum proves the other approximation inequality. This proves every assertion above.

assumptions: There is L>0 such that |f(u)-f(v)|<=L||u-v|| for all u,v in X.
beta>0; the prox is the exact constrained minimizer over X.
statement.conclusion: E_beta is differentiable on R^d, grad E_beta(x)=beta(x-p_beta(x)), and ||grad E_beta(x)-grad E_beta(y)||<=beta||x-y|| for all x,y in R^d. For every x in X, E_beta(x)<=f(x)<=E_beta(x)+L^2/(2beta).
statement.objects_and_definitions: Use the Euclidean norm on R^d. For a nonempty closed convex X and finite f:X->R, define E_beta(x)=inf_{u in X}[f(u)+(beta/2)||x-u||^2] for every x in R^d, and p_beta(x) as its minimizer.
statement.parameter_domains: d is a positive integer; L,beta are positive real numbers. X may be unbounded or lower dimensional.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every finite dimension d>=1, every such X,f,L, every beta>0 and every x in R^d, the minimizer exists uniquely and the gradient formula holds. Smoothness is global on R^d. The approximation inequalities are asserted for every x in X. There is no randomness.

summary: With the paper's quadratic-penalty convention, the constrained Moreau envelope has beta-Lipschitz gradient and bias at most L^2/(2beta) on X. A complete local reconstruction is supplied separately from the source statement.
